title: Music for gamedev
author: PhotoDisastrous8275
selftext:
What's the consensus for AI generated music in video games.  
I have tried to keep the art side of my game AI free because I know how it can impact sales but I'm at a point now were I need music for my game and nothing out there fits my needs. The things that do are extremely expensive and I would definitely eventually buy it over time but its simply not affordable for me right now.

I know statistically games with AI art disclosures usually perform worse, so I wanted to get your take

comments.author: Sigilscape
comments.body: I use suno because it gives me copywrite free orchestral pieces

replies.author: PhotoDisastrous8275
replies.body: That’s exactly what I need as well and it makes some really good ones too. So the quality isn’t the issue. It’s the public’s reaction which I’m unsure about

replies.author: Sigilscape
replies.body: The majority wont care, the loud minority will try to make you feel like you've murdered someone. Ultimately do what makes you happy

replies.author: My0Cents
replies.body:
You can make AI generated instrumental music that is indistinguishable from human made music using correct prompting and post processing. Ask Claude for help. Currently in music, it's always the vocals that are the dead AI giveaway.

However you're kinda obligated to disclose that it's AI generated. You just have to make it not sound AI generated and almost no one will care.

comments.author: Gelinhir
comments.body: Ai music is horrible unless YOU are a music producer in the first place and use AI for support not just make everything with it.

comments.author: cristocanaro
comments.body: Suno is great. I’ve been working in the big industry! They use it too, can’t disclose companies though

replies.author: PhotoDisastrous8275
replies.body: Yeah after days of looking for tracks. I went on Suno just to see and with one prompt it made a track that was just as good as the composed tracks I wanted to purchase but were to expensive for me at the moment

comments.author: Braunb8888
comments.body: Scoring my own game, but happy to dm you about this if you’re looking for someone to do the same for your game. 20 year guitar player here. I just mess with the sound types to get what I want after I play it.

comments.author: GCC_GicaCamelCase
comments.body: I am all pro AI, but I guess music is too personal to me, or somehow some AI music gives me the uncanny valley vibes and it's a huge turnoff. You can find a lot of royalty free music out there.

replies.author: o_nee_san
replies.body: Agreed. Nothing against AI. I just built a couple of minimalist puzzle games and I couldn’t even get a decent bubble popping sound, let alone a soundtrack. I ended up going to freesound. Free to use as long as you credit the creator of the sound (which I would do anyway).

comments.author: FallenWyvern
comments.body:
[https://www.humblebundle.com/software/complete-works-massive-collection-royaltyfree-audio-tracks-software](https://www.humblebundle.com/software/complete-works-massive-collection-royaltyfree-audio-tracks-software)

  
Oh look, hundreds of royalty free songs for use in video games! And your money goes to a good cause. I'm not saying one way or another about AI music, but this is a very cheap way to get some good tracks

replies.author: PhotoDisastrous8275
replies.body:
Im looking through them and so far nothing fits what I'm looking for.  
Again I looked for Human composed music first and what I found that could be used for my game would run me 1k +. My next step if i dont find anything is to use Suno and replace it with human composed music little by little.

replies.author: FallenWyvern
replies.body:
Ok as someone who bought that pack, each of those has a minimum 8-10 songs. There are 128 items.

ACross 1000+ songs you found none of them are right for you?

What about public domain/CC music? 

Pixabay has some: https://pixabay.com/music/search/cc0/

There's some classical public domain cc0 stuff here: https://www.chosic.com/free-music/all/?attribution=no

FreePD has CC0: https://en.freepd.cn/music

Nullrights has CC0: https://nullrights.com/

And then in videos on youtube I've used music from these artists who were kind enough to just release their music into public domain:

https://icons8.com/music/author/krope
https://soundcloud.com/ithacastudio
https://soundcloud.com/scottbuckley/sets/creative-commons-music-library
https://icons8.com/music/search/ilya-truhanov
https://soundcloud.com/stevenobrien/sets/creative-commons-favorites

replies.author: PhotoDisastrous8275
replies.body:
I only  
Listened to the category I was looking for in that pack which eliminated around 90 percent of the other music. 

I’ll take a look at the other links you sent.

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body: I've found that most people cant tell. They have to be exposed to a lot of it to tell. Vocals is usually the give away and most game music doesnt use vocals so it comes in safe. Suno is the major provider, just read their TOS very closely, it has some gotchas in it.

comments.author: Agile_Branch_8743
comments.body: There's plenty of free to use or cheap music you can use in your projects that will be better than most stuff an AI generates.

replies.author: PhotoDisastrous8275
replies.body: Yeah that’s not really true. The tracks generated by suno are just as good or better than the premium tracks I was looking to purchase. As far as free or cheap music for the genre I was looking for there is nothing that works for my game

comments.author: thvaz
comments.body: I used Suno and honestly, there is no way I could have that quality with my budget. I thought it turned out great.

comments.author: taddeimania
comments.body: If you'd like a more hands on approach for scoring music with your AI - you could take a look at a tool I built for recording / scoring music, but it has an MCP integration you can wire your agent into and set it loose on writing music for, or with you.  [https://getlathe.app/ai.html](https://getlathe.app/ai.html) It's free to use, and the cloud sync (currently in beta) is the only thing that'll probably be a paid thing, but it won't stop you from using the DAW.

replies.body:
I know it's super basic, but I told Claude (wired into the MCP) to author a generic techno beat at 143bpm that I could use in a product trailer and it made this 100% on its own.

[https://getlathe.app/listen.html#KfT11i1tmbx0Ap7O](https://getlathe.app/listen.html#KfT11i1tmbx0Ap7O)

comments.author: tindalos
comments.body:
Don’t buy into the hate or fear, it’s temporary.   Ai enables what you can envision but can’t do (yet), so if you can’t write or hire someone to perform your own songs to fit what you want, use Ai as that’s what it does well and gives the player the best experience, if it’s done right.  

What people don’t recognize is they’re two sides of the same coin and both have different levels of practice and iteration to refine, whether it’s art or music, human or Ai.  

If you’re using any Ai you’re going to get some dogmatic hate these days but it’ll fade, and Ai art and music have the ability to bring something different than human music does, so lean into those quirks.   Don’t degrade your vision of your game because someone thinks you should be building your own house to live in these days.   

The goal is still to use whatever tools and budget you can to make the best vision you have to create an engaging experience for the player.   Ai makes that easier to do for a solo dev or small team, but that means you should spend the time to get it right - the way you see it in your head.

Let the haters hate, because in time it’ll mean a lot more that you made the game you wanted instead of the areas you cut from peer pressure.

comments.author: guanzo91
comments.body: I tried getting Claude to actually compose music for me because I wanted control over the melodies, but the output was just so generic and uninspiring.
